title: Normalization geonormal insep
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There exists a finite purely inseparable extension $k\subseteq k'$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] such that the normalization $N$ of $X_{k'}=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is geometrically normal over $k'$: for every extension field $L/k'$, every local ring of $N_L$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Here normalization means the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of the reduced irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family].

proof.text: Take K = perfectClosure k (AlgebraicClosure k). Apply the finite-model statement to obtain a finite intermediate field E, finite surjective model f:Y to X_E and dense open U whose inverse image in Y is dense, with restricted f a closed immersion and normal K-base change. K/E is perfect and purely inseparable by the power criterion. The perfect-closure normality test gives normal domain stalks after every field extension of E. Its specialization to E, transported through the trivial self-base-change isomorphism, gives normal stalks on Y itself.

Set T=X_E. Finite type over E makes T Noetherian, so its components are finite. Each reduced component C_Z is integral by the componentwise normalization definition. Its normalization is finite over T by the source theorem Scheme.isFinite_fromNormalization_of_locallyOfFiniteType and composition with its closed inclusion. Their finite coproduct is finite by IsFinite.sigmaDesc. Its stalks are normal domains by Scheme.Hom.isIntegrallyClosed_stalk_normalization over a function field, and transport along the open coprojections.

The inverse image of U in each integral component normalization is nonempty. Indeed the complement W of the other finitely many components is open with closure that component. W is nonempty and intersects dense U; lift a point of this intersection through the closed component and its surjective normalization. The inverse image is therefore nonempty open in an irreducible normalization, hence dense. Continuity of the coprojections then proves density in the entire coproduct. This is the explicit Lean proof reducedNormalization_dense_preimage, including the empty coproduct case.

The normal stalks make Y reduced. The restricted map f inverse U to U is a surjective closed immersion from a reduced scheme. Its canonical factorization through U_red is itself a closed immersion (cancellation of closed immersions), surjective by injectivity of U_red to U, and thus an isomorphism since U_red is reduced. This is the explicit Lean helper reduced_closedImmersion_iso. Transfer the normal stalks of the open f inverse U to U_red. The local normalization compatibility statement now identifies N inverse U with U_red, so composing gives an isomorphism with f inverse U over U. Finally both maps are finite over locally Noetherian T, both sources have normal domain stalks, and both preimages of U are dense. The existing finite-normal dense-open comparison gives N isomorphic to Y over T.

Choose an equivalence Fin n with the finite type of irreducible components of T. Take each C_i to be its reduced induced subscheme and its closed inclusion. The range equation for vanishing-ideal subschemes proves both distinctness and exhaustive enumeration. Sigma.whiskerEquiv reindexes the componentwise normalization coproduct and preserves its map to T. Compose with the isomorphism to Y. For each extension L/E, pullback.map along this isomorphism is an isomorphism over Spec L; its stalk isomorphisms transfer normal-domain assertions from Y_L to the specified coproduct base change. This supplies exactly the unchanged conclusion.
